issues.failure_explanation: The proof splits G=[B,(x+y)gamma]^T[B,(x+y)gamma] = diag(B^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2) + offdiag(gamma B^Ty) (correct), but then works with diag(B^TB, 1) + [[0, gamma B^Ty],[gamma y^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2]], whose (2,2) entry sums to 1 + gamma^2||x+y||^2, not gamma^2||x+y||^2. The subsequent bounds lambda_max <= sigma_max^2(B) + lambda_max(A) and lambda_min >= sigma_min^2(B) + lambda_min(A) also silently need sigma_max(B) >= 1 and sigma_min(B) <= 1, which are not assumed. The stated inequalities are in fact false: with B=[1;0] in R^2, x=(0,1) in span(B^perp), y=(1,-1/2), gamma=1, b=x+y=(1,1/2), kappa([B,b]) = kappa([[1,1],[0,1/2]]) = sqrt(2.133/0.117) ~= 4.27, while item 1's right side is sqrt(5.61/0.89) ~= 2.51; as y's component along span(B) shrinks, dist(b,span(B)) -> 0 with ||x+y|| and ||B^Ty|| bounded, so kappa([B,b]) -> infinity while the bound stays finite, so no finite bound of this form can hold without assumptions. Item 2 also fails: with B orthonormal 3x2 (kappa(B)=1), x=e3, y=e1, u=(x+y)/||x+y||, the hypothesis ||B^Ty||/||x+y|| = 1/sqrt(2) <= (eps^2-1)/4 holds at eps=2, but kappa([B,u]) = 1+sqrt(2) ~ 2.414 > kappa(B)*sqrt(1+f(B,2)) = sqrt(5) ~ 2.236.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $Z_1 \sim \chi^2_n$, $Z_2 \sim \chi'^2_{m-n}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2^2}{\sigma^2}\right)$, therefore, by Chapter 6, equation 40 of \cite{patnaik1949non}, we have:

issues.failure_explanation: Z1 and Z2 are Euclidean norms, so Z1^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_n and Z2^2/sigma^2 ~ chi'^2_{m-n}(lambda) with lambda = ||X||^2/sigma^2; the noncentral F statistic is (Z2^2/(m-n))/(Z1^2/n). The proof instead asserts 'Z1 ~ chi^2_n' and treats (Z2/(m-n))/(Z1/n) = (n/(m-n)) Z2/Z1 as noncentral-F distributed, which is false (a ratio of chi, not chi-squared, variables). The correct identity is P(||r||_2 >= 1/sqrt(1+(eps1/eps2)^2)) = F'_{m-n,n}( n eps2^2 / ((m-n) eps1^2) ; ||X||^2/sigma^2 ). Counterexample: m = 2, n = 1, X = 0, sigma = 1, eps1 = 2, eps2 = 1: the left side is P(F_{1,1} > 4) ~ 0.295, the stated right side is the survival of F_{1,1} at 1/2, ~ 0.61.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Form the F statistic from Z2^2 and Z1^2, i.e. change the argument to n*eps2^2/((m-n)*eps1^2) and state the chi-squared variables as Z1^2, Z2^2; a one-step correction of the final inference, applied also in the two dependent corollaries.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's stated probability is wrong for eps1 != eps2; the same erroneous F' argument is reused verbatim in Corollary cor-main and Corollary cor:added-2, so their stated confidence levels are also wrong.
issues.title: Theorem thm:noise-ls: final F' identity uses norms where chi-squared variables are required, giving a wrong F argument
issues.why_classification: A local, forced recalibration of one displayed formula restores a true theorem of the same form and scope, with the same one-step fix propagated to its two dependents.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem defines ||r||_2 as the residual norm for target c*gamma, but then cites Liesen et al.'s formula kappa([Q,c*gamma]) = (alpha + sqrt(alpha^2 - 4 gamma^2 ||r||^2))/(2 gamma ||r||), which is parameterized by the residual of c (as the paper's own Theorem thm:strak states: ||r||_2 = min_u ||c - Bu||_2). With the theorem's definition ||r|| = gamma*||r_c||, the correct bound is kappa([B,c*gamma]) <= kappa(B)(alpha + sqrt(alpha^2 - 4||r||^2))/(2||r||); the displayed formula is false for gamma != 1: with B = [1;0] (unit columns), c = (1,1), gamma = 2, kappa([B,2c]) = kappa([[1,2],[0,2]]) ~ 4.27 while the stated right side is (9 + sqrt(17))/8 ~ 1.64. For gamma < 0 the right side is negative while kappa > 0.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary never defines q. Combining its two cited results gives, with rho = eps1/eps2 and s = ||r||_2, kappa([B,q]) <= kappa(B)(1+sqrt(1-s^2))/s <= kappa(B)(sqrt(1+rho^2) + rho) on the event s >= 1/sqrt(1+rho^2), not kappa(B)*eps1*sqrt(1+rho^2).
